item.title: Rampal cluster village struggles with multiple problems
item.description:
A cluster village established for families displaced by the Rampal Thermal Power Plant is facing severe waterlogging, inadequate public services and barriers to education, with residents blaming poor infrastructure for deteriorating living conditions and an increase in child marriages.
Located at Kaigaddaskathi behind the power plant, the village is home to around 800 families, although only 142 households have received government-built houses.
Residents say an earthen embankment constructed around the village has trapped rainwater and household wastewater because no drainage system was built, leaving the area submerged for nearly nine months each year.
The prolonged waterlogging has created unhygienic conditions, with overflowing toilets and stagnant water contributing to widespread skin diseases, including rashes and itching among children and adults.
"We have nowhere for the water to go," said Rafiza Begum. "When it rains, the toilets overflow and we are forced to walk through dirty water."
Residents said they had previously lived on khas land before it was acquired for the power plant. Each family was later allocated 1.75 decimals of land on a nearby river char for rehabilitation. Initially, all lived in makeshift shelters before some received permanent houses under government housing programmes.
Parents say access to education has become one of the settlement's biggest challenges.
Although a primary school is located nearby, there is no secondary school within six kilometres, forcing students either to travel to Borni or cross the river to Chalna.
For many families, particularly those with daughters, the journey is considered unsafe and too costly.
"As parents, we worry about our daughters travelling such long distances," said Asiya Begum. "Transport costs are high and crossing the river is risky. Many families end up arranging marriages instead."
Residents claim at least 15 child marriages have taken place in the settlement over the past two years, citing poverty, insecurity and limited educational opportunities as key factors.
Residents also say healthcare remains difficult to access despite living close to the power plant.
According to them, reaching the hospital associated with the project requires travelling 15 to 16 kilometres because of poor road connectivity and limited transport services. As a result, many rely on the health centre across the river in Chalna.
Ershad Ali said families who lost land to the project have received few long-term economic benefits.
"Our land was acquired, but local people have not found jobs at the power plant," he said. "We are also facing an acute shortage of safe drinking water."
In neighbouring Kapasdanga village, resident Ila Devi said there are three primary schools within three kilometres but no nearby secondary school.
She said it costs around Tk50 a day for one student to travel to school, an expense many low-income families cannot afford.
"I can only send my daughter to school twice a week," she said.
Riya Mondal said girls travelling to the secondary school in Chalna often have to wade through knee-deep saline water during high tide before boarding a ferry.
"They attend classes in wet clothes after crossing the river," she said. "Many parents do not want to take that risk."
Rampal Upazila Nirbahi Officer Tamanna Ferdousi said child marriage could not be justified under any circumstances.
"The area may not have been under adequate monitoring," she said. "Necessary steps will be taken through the Department of Women's Affairs to strengthen monitoring and prevent child marriage."
Responding to complaints of waterlogging, the UNO said no formal complaint had previously reached the administration but added that the matter would be investigated through the relevant project officials and necessary measures taken if required.

item.title: Pineapple farming takes root in Naogaon mango orchards
item.description:
Pineapple cultivation is gaining momentum in Naogaon’s Barind region as farmers are using vacant spaces between mango trees to grow the sweet fruit as an intercrop, creating new economic opportunities for the area.
The soil and climatic conditions of Porsha, Sapahar, and Patnitala upazilas are considered highly suitable for pineapple farming, with the region’s land consisting mainly of loamy and sandy-loamy soil. As pineapple cultivation requires relatively low investment while offering good returns, it is adding a new dimension to the rural economy.
Farmers are now cultivating MB-2 and Honey Queen varieties of pineapple in the unused spaces of mango orchards. It takes around 15 to 18 months from planting saplings to harvesting fruit. By producing two crops from the same land, farmers are improving land utilisation and increasing their income.
Due to favourable yields, pineapples grown in Naogaon are meeting local demand and are also being supplied to different parts of the country. Once established, pineapple plants can continue producing fruit for several years with minimal additional costs. The pineapples produced in the region are gaining popularity for their sweetness and distinctive taste.
Young agricultural entrepreneur Rayhan Siddiq of Porsha has become the first person in Naogaon to achieve commercial success through pineapple cultivation.
Rayhan said he planted 3,000 pineapple saplings collected from the Badalgachhi Horticulture Centre in 2024 during the rainy season. “After planting, I did not need to provide any irrigation. I only removed weeds and applied pesticides a few times. The pineapples have grown with very little expense,” he said.
He has already sold pineapples worth Tk 10,000 and expects to sell additional fruits worth around Tk 100,000. “The biggest advantage is that mangoes and pineapples can be cultivated on the same land. The cost is very low, and the fruits are extremely tasty,” he added.
Rayhan said he plans to expand pineapple cultivation on a larger scale. “We usually bring pineapples from Tangail and other districts to meet local demand. If pineapple farming expands in this mango-growing region, we will be able to fulfil the district’s demand with locally produced fruits,” he said.
Young agricultural entrepreneur Abdus Sobhan from Manda visited Rayhan’s farm after hearing that pineapple cultivation had started in Naogaon for the first time. “Rayhan Bhai offered me pineapple from his farm. It was very sweet. I have decided to start pineapple cultivation as well,” he said.
Another visitor, Tasnim, said she had never seen pineapple cultivation in Naogaon before. “I came after hearing about it and tasted the fruit. The flavour was amazing. I never imagined pineapples from this region could be so sweet,” she said.
Fruit trader Yasin Ali said they conduct fruit trading throughout the year. “Rayhan Bhai is the first person to cultivate pineapples commercially in this district. We came to buy his fruits. The production is good, and the market price is also encouraging,” he said.
Motahar Mia, a worker who has long been employed at Rayhan’s mango orchard, now also takes care of the pineapple plants. He believes Naogaon’s soil is highly suitable for pineapple cultivation.
Porsha Upazila Sub-Assistant Agriculture Officer Samirul Islam said Rayhan’s pineapple cultivation in a mango orchard is an excellent example of intercrop farming. “He is the first farmer in the district to commercially cultivate pineapples between mango trees. The growth of the plants and the quality of the fruits are very good,” he said.
Samirul added that expanding pineapple cultivation alongside mango orchards could create a new economic opportunity for the region. “The first harvest comes after 15 to 18 months. After that, the plants bear fruit every year without requiring replanting. Each plant produces four to five crowns, which can be sold as saplings or planted elsewhere,” he said.
He also said the agriculture department is providing overall support to Rayhan to encourage pineapple cultivation across the district.

item.title: Dengue: One more death, 546 new cases in 24 hours
item.description:
Health authorities on Monday reported 546 new dengue cases and 1 death recorded in the past 24 hours, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
A DGHS statement said that, of the 546 newly hospitalized patients, 96 were admitted in Barisal division, 97 in Chittagong division, 109 in Dhaka division, 56 in Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC), 58 in Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC), 65 in Khulna division, 24 in Mymensingh division, 32 in Rajshahi division, and 9 in Rangpur division.
With the latest figures, the country's dengue death toll this year has reached 44, while the total number of reported cases has risen to 13,644.
Last year, dengue claimed 413 lives and infected 102,861 people across the country.
In 2024, the mosquito-borne disease caused 575 deaths and infected 101,214 people.

item.title: Writ seeks HC probe into microplastics in 26 toothpaste brands in Bangladesh
item.description:
A writ petition has been filed with the High Court seeking an investigation into reports that 26 of 34 toothpaste products available in the Bangladeshi market contain potentially harmful microplastics.
Supreme Court lawyer Md Abdullah Al Mamun filed the petition on Monday.
The respondents include the secretaries of the Ministries of Health, Environment and Commerce, along with the Bangladesh Standards and Testing Institution (BSTI) and the Directorate of National Consumer Rights Protection (DNCRP).
The petition cites published media reports, which said microplastics were detected in 26 of the 34 toothpaste samples tested. The concentration of plastic particles ranged from 20 to 320 per 100 grams of toothpaste. The reports also said microplastics were found in four of the six toothpaste products formulated for children.
The findings were revealed in a recent study by the Environment and Social Development Organization (ESDO), which warned that the presence of microplastics in toothpaste poses potential risks to both human health and the environment.
According to the study, conducted between July 2025 and June 2026, researchers analysed 34 toothpaste samples representing 19 major brands manufactured in Bangladesh, India, Thailand and Vietnam.
Of the 25 locally manufactured samples, 22 were found to contain microplastics. Among the imported products, microplastics were detected in one of the five samples from India, one of the two samples from Thailand, and both samples imported from Vietnam.

item.title: Home minister: Govt prioritizes secure environment for investors
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Monday said the government has prioritized creating a secure and stable environment for both domestic and foreign investors.
He made the remarks while speaking as the special guest at the foundation stone-laying ceremony of the China Economic and Industrial Zone (CEIZ) in Anwara, Chittagong.
Salahuddin Ahmed said law enforcement agencies would ensure security throughout every phase of the project and take all necessary measures to maintain safe communication systems and uninterrupted operations.
He said the Bangladesh Economic Zones Authority (BEZA) has introduced a one-stop service to create an investment-friendly environment.
“This initiative will provide investors with prompt approvals, straightforward utility connections, and essential administrative assistance. The government is committed to fulfilling every commitment made under the G2G agreement in a timely, transparent, and efficient manner,” he said.
The home minister said the industrial zone would create new opportunities for employment, skills development, and economic growth for local communities.
“It represents not merely an industrial zone but also a conduit for a long-term economic partnership between Bangladesh and China. This project will be pivotal in promoting sustainable industrialization and building a prosperous Bangladesh for future generations,” he added.
Salahuddin Ahmed also said the initiative reflects the enduring friendship, mutual trust, and strategic partnership between Bangladesh and China, while opening new opportunities in industrial production, global supply chains, technology transfer, and skilled human resource development.
Finance Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury, State Minister for Land Mir Mohammed Helal Uddin, Chinese Ambassador to Bangladesh Yao Wen, Bangladesh Economic Zones Authority Executive Chairman Chowdhury Ashiq Mahmud Bin Harun, China Economic and Industrial Zone Chairman Wang Benchian, and representatives from the public and private sectors of both countries attended the program.

item.title: DMP urges Dhaka residents to register with CIMS
item.description:
Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has urged homeowners, tenants and mess (shared accommodation) members in the capital to register with the Citizen Information Management System (CIMS), saying the platform will strengthen technology-based policing and enhance public safety.
The digital information management system registers, stores and updates the basic information of homeowners, tenants and mess members living in Dhaka.
DMP launched the software-based CIMS at Ramna Police Station on September 1, 2016. The system was expanded to all police stations across the capital in 2017, while the CIMS mobile app was introduced in 2019 to simplify the registration process.
According to DMP, 3,673,238 households have been registered in the CIMS database, which contains information on more than 5 million citizens. Police said the registration process is ongoing and urged all residents of the capital to enroll.
Why register with CIMS
DMP said CIMS helps maintain accurate and up-to-date citizen information, making beat policing more effective. The database also supports crime prevention and investigation, assists in identifying missing persons, verifies the identities of suspected individuals and enables the rapid collection and use of information during emergencies.
How to register
CIMS registration forms are available at every police station and police outpost within the Dhaka metropolitan area. Citizens can collect a form, complete it and submit it to the relevant police station. DMP advises applicants to keep a photocopy of the completed form for their records before submitting it.
Each DMP police station is divided into multiple beats, with a designated beat officer assigned to each area. Residents may contact their respective beat officer for assistance whenever necessary.
If a resident changes address, they must register again with the police station responsible for their new address.
Benefits for homeowners and tenants
DMP said homeowners can use CIMS registration to verify the identities of prospective tenants, reducing the risk of criminals or fraudsters renting or taking shelter on their premises and helping them avoid unnecessary harassment.
For tenants, registration provides an opportunity to become acquainted with their local beat officer, receive police assistance more quickly when needed and benefit from identity verification.
Role in crime prevention
According to DMP, the CIMS database plays an important role in criminal investigations by helping identify absconding criminals, verify information on suspected individuals and support timely crime prevention efforts.
Police also said the system has strengthened beat policing and helped build greater trust between law enforcement agencies and the public.
DMP's appeal
The Dhaka Metropolitan Police has called on all homeowners, tenants and mess members in the capital to complete their CIMS registration to help build a safer and crime-free Dhaka.

item.title: PM joins Notun Kuri sports grand finale
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Monday joined the grand finale of the national-level Notun Kuri Sports 2025-26 at the Bangladesh Army Stadium in Dhaka.
The nationwide sporting event, organized under the supervision of the Ministry of Youth and Sports, was held with the theme: "Krira Hole Pesha, Paribar Pabe Bharosha (If sports becomes a profession, family will find security)."
The prime minister arrived at the venue at 4pm and was greeted by thousands of young spectators. He waved to the crowd, exchanged greetings with athletes on the field, and interacted with students in the galleries, encouraging them to pursue sports. More than 8,000 students attended the event.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed and State Minister for Youth and Sports Md Aminul Haque accompanied the prime minister.
The Notun Kuri Sports program was launched on May 2 at Sylhet District Stadium with the aim of identifying sporting talent among boys and girls aged 12 to 14 and encouraging grassroots participation in sports.
According to the organizers, around 170,000 athletes from districts and upazilas across the country competed in the regional phase across 8 disciplines before advancing to the national-level competitions held in Dhaka.
This year's edition featured football, cricket, kabaddi, athletics, badminton, chess, swimming, and martial arts.
The closing ceremony included the boys' and girls' football finals and the boys' and girls' 100-meter sprint events.
In the boys' football final, Sylhet Region defeated Mymensingh Region 2-0.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman was scheduled to distribute trophies and prizes to the winners during the award ceremony beginning at 5pm.

Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 825 as five die in 24 hours
item.description:
Five more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Monday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 825.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all five of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 730, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 95, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the five new suspected fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in Dhaka, with three deaths reported in both the Dhaka division and Dhaka district.
A total of 992 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Monday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 124,745.
During the same period, 113 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 15,555.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 107,654 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 103,467 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Man killed in train accident at Tejgaon
item.description:
An unidentified man was killed after being struck by a train at Tejgaon Railway Station in Dhaka on Monday morning. His identity could not be established.
The deceased was estimated to be around 35 years old. He was wearing a blue full-sleeved shirt and a lungi.
Dhaka Railway Police Station Sub-Inspector Rafiqul Islam said: “An unidentified man was killed on the spot after being hit by a train at the end of Platform No 1 of Tejgaon Railway Station on Monday morning. After receiving the information, police recovered the body from the spot at around 8:45am. Following legal procedures, the body has been sent to the morgue of Dhaka Medical College Hospital for an autopsy.”
He added that efforts are underway to identify the deceased.

item.description:

item.title: Fakhrul: Presidential election to be held on time
item.description:
The presidential election will be held on time and candidates for the post will be nominated according to the party’s decision, LGRD Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir said on Monday.
He made the remarks while responding to journalists' questions after inaugurating the divisional office of the Bangladesh Rural Development Board (BRDB) in the Terminal area of Rangpur city.
Mirza Fakhrul said the BNP is a democratic political party.
“Through a long struggle, our party formed the government with a two-thirds majority in parliament with the love and votes of the people,” he said.
He said the BNP had fulfilled the responsibility of running the government not once, but five times. “Those who call BNP a fascist either lack knowledge or have developed such a mentality,” he added.
The minister also urged the Jamaat-e-Islami ameer to read his party’s constitution carefully and assess how democratic the party is.
Regarding local government elections, he said the Election Commission would decide on the issue of educational qualifications for candidates. “If not by the end of this year, the local government elections will be held early next year,” he said.
Mirza Fakhrul also said the government has waived interest on agricultural loans up to Tk10,000 to support agricultural development.
He added that the prime minister announced maximum allocation for agricultural development in the Rangpur region and that all necessary steps would be taken to make agriculture profitable.
Later, Mirza Fakhrul inaugurated a rural fair organised at the Rangpur Public Library grounds, visited different stalls and attended a community meeting at the Shilpakala Academy.
Rangpur Development Authority Chairman Shamsuzzaman Samu, Divisional Commissioner Shahidul Islam (NDC), Rangpur Range DIG Aminul Islam, Rangpur Deputy Commissioner Ruhul Amin, Rangpur Zilla Parishad Administrator Saiful Islam, government officials and employees, and BNP leaders and activists were present.

item.title: Shapla Chattar case: Tribunal issues arrest warrants for Hasina, others
item.description:
The International Crimes Tribunal (ICT)-2 on Monday took cognizance of formal charges against 41 people, including fugitive former prime minister Sheikh Hasina and former army chief Gen Aziz Ahmed, in a case over alleged crimes against humanity linked to the May 5, 2013, crackdown on a Hefazat-e-Islam rally at Shapla Chattar in Motijheel.
The three-member tribunal, headed by Justice Nazrul Islam, also issued arrest warrants against Sheikh Hasina and the other fugitive accused after hearing the prosecution's application.
Among those for whom arrest warrants were issued are former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, former army chief Gen Aziz Ahmed and former inspector general of police (IGP) Benazir Ahmed.
Nine accused are currently in custody in the case. They are former minister Dr Dipu Moni, former state minister for home affairs Shamsul Hoque Tuku, retired Maj Gen Ziaul Ahsan, former IGP AKM Shahidul Haque, former deputy inspector general (DIG) Molla Nazrul Islam, Ekattorer Ghatak Dalal Nirmul Committee advisory council chairman Shahriar Kabir, former DIG Abdul Jalil Mondol, and journalists Farzana Rupa and Mozammel Babu.
Prosecutors Zahirul Amin, Moinul Karim and Marjina Raihan represented the prosecution during the submission of the formal charges.
The charge sheet also names former home minister Dr Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir, former information ministers Hasanul Haq Inu and Dr Hasan Mahmud, former food minister Dr Abdur Razzaque, Awami League leaders Sheikh Fazlul Karim Selim, Mahbubul Alam Hanif, AFM Bahauddin Nasim and Jahangir Kabir Nanak, former ministers Abdul Latif Siddiqui, Mofazzal Hossain Chowdhury Maya and Dr Dipu Moni, former Jubo League chairman Omar Faruk Chowdhury, former MP Salauddin Mahmud, Jana Jagaran Mancha spokesperson Dr Imran H Sarker, Ekattorer Ghatak Dalal Nirmul Committee president Shahriar Kabir, 71 TV Managing Director Mozammel Haque Babu, journalist Farzana Rupa, several former police chiefs and senior police officials, as well as former RAB and army officers.
On May 5, 2013, Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh held a rally at Shapla Chattar in Motijheel to press its 13-point demands. Following daylong tensions and clashes, police, the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) carried out a joint operation overnight to clear the area.
The International Crimes Tribunal later launched an investigation into allegations that many people were killed during the operation.

item.title: Amit: Gas supply to improve from next week, return to normalcy a week later
item.description:
State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Aninda Islam Amit on Monday once again apologized to the public for the ongoing gas crisis, expressing hope that supply will begin to improve from next week, with full restoration expected about a week later.
Speaking to reporters at his office at the Secretariat, he said the government is making every possible effort to resolve the crisis, which has severely affected households, industries and transport services.
"We know homemakers are struggling to cook, industries have had to scale back production, and pressure on CNG stations has disrupted public transport. We sincerely apologies to the people for the hardship," the state minister said.
He said the disruption was not caused by any government agency but stemmed from a problem involving a private operator responsible for ensuring part of the country's gas supply.
"We are working jointly with them around the clock. We cannot provide an immediate solution due to certain limitations. However, our teams are working 24/7 with the company, and we hope the situation will start improving from next week, InshaAllah," Amit said.
Referring to the floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU) in Moheshkhali of Cox’s Bazar where the technical fault occurred, he said the facility normally supplies around 500 to 550 million cubic feet of gas per day.
According to information provided by the operator, the state minister said, the FSRU is expected to resume supplying around 280 to 300 million cubic feet of gas per day to the national grid from next week.
"If they can restore about 50% of the supply next week, the plan is to return to 100 percent capacity in the following week," he added.

item.title: Dismissed police personnel seek PM's intervention for reinstatement
item.description:
A group of dismissed police personnel on Monday urged the prime minister to intervene and ensure their reinstatement, claiming they were removed from service during the Awami League government's tenure due to political persecution rather than proven misconduct.
They made the demand during a human chain program held in front of the Jatiya Press Club in the capital.
Speaking at the program, representatives of the dismissed personnel said they were among 1,522 police officers and employees who had either been dismissed or forced into retirement without fair departmental inquiries.
They alleged that the previous government removed hundreds of honest and competent police personnel to serve political interests and suppress dissent.
According to the protesters, after the change in government, they appealed to the interim government for justice.
They claimed the home ministry later issued an order supporting their reinstatement on humanitarian grounds.
Following the ministry's decision, Police Headquarters formed a 10-member high-level committee, led by a Deputy Inspector General (DIG), to review the cases, they said. The committee reportedly examined the matter over six months before submitting four recommendations.
They also said Police Headquarters' media cell announced through the media on February 8, 2025, that the 1,522 dismissed police personnel would soon be reinstated, raising hopes among the affected members and their families.
However, they alleged that despite the Home Ministry's order, the committee's findings and the public announcement, the reinstatement process has yet to be implemented.
The protesters further claimed there had been inconsistencies in implementing the committee's recommendations. They alleged that although the committee recommended reinstating only those who had received two favorable verdicts from the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, some personnel with only one favorable verdict were later allowed to return to service.
Addressing the gathering, former Sub-Inspector Mamun Sirajul Haque urged the prime minister to ensure implementation of the home ministry's reinstatement order and the Police Headquarters committee's recommendations, expressing hope that the affected 1,522 families would be able to regain their livelihoods and return to serving the country.

item.title: Freedom fighter allowances increased from July 1
item.description:
The government has increased the monthly honorarium and other financial benefits for freedom fighters, families of martyred freedom fighters and war-wounded freedom fighters.
The revised rates, announced in a notification issued by the Budget Branch of the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs, will take effect from July 1, 2026.
Under the new rates, monthly honorariums, festival allowances, medical allowances and special grants for Victory Day and the Bangla New Year have been increased for various categories of freedom fighters and their families. Benefits for families of martyred freedom fighters have also been raised.
The ministry said the decision was taken under Section 3 of the Bangladesh Freedom Fighters Welfare Trust Act, 2018, and the relevant rules framed by the ministry, with the aim of strengthening the welfare, dignity and social security of freedom fighters.
Under the revised structure, recipients of the Bir Uttam title will receive a monthly honorarium of Tk30,000, along with Tk10,000 as a festival allowance, Tk5,000 on Victory Day and Tk2,000 for the Bangla New Year.
Recipients of the Bir Bikram and Bir Protik titles will receive a monthly honorarium of Tk25,000, as well as Tk10,000 in festival allowance, Tk5,000 for Victory Day and Tk2,000 for the Bangla New Year.
Families of martyred freedom fighters will receive a monthly honorarium of Tk23,000, a Tk2,000 medical allowance, a Tk5,000 food allowance, a festival allowance of Tk23,000 and Tk2,000 for the Bangla New Year.
The government has also revised monthly honorariums for war-wounded freedom fighters based on disability categories. Category A (96-100% disability) beneficiaries will receive Tk30,000 per month, Category B (61-95%) Tk28,000, Category C (20-60%) Tk23,000, and Category D (1-19%) Tk20,000.
The notification, signed by Deputy Secretary Dr Md Asaduzzaman, said the government is continuing to implement welfare programs to strengthen the financial security and social status of freedom fighters and their families. Source: BSS.

Shapla Chattar case: Prosecution files charges against Hasina, 40 others
item.description:
The prosecution has filed formal charges against ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina and 40 others in a crimes against humanity case over the killings during the Hefazat-e-Islam rally at Shapla Chattar in Dhaka's Motijheel in 2013.
Prosecutor Zahirul Amin submitted the formal charges to the registrar of the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) at around 10:45am on Monday. Prosecutor Marzina Raihan was also present.
A hearing in the case is scheduled to be held later in the day before a three-member bench of ICT-1 headed by Justice Md Golam Mortuza Majumder.
According to prosecution sources, the investigation report names 41 accused, including former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, former army chief General Aziz Ahmed, journalists Mozammel Babu and Farzana Rupa, and writer Shahriar Kabir.
On May 5, 2013, Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh staged a rally at Shapla Chattar in Dhaka's Motijheel, demanding implementation of its 13-point charter.
Following a day of tensions and clashes, members of the police, Rapid Action Battalion (RAB), and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) carried out a joint overnight operation to clear the area.
Allegations that numerous people were killed during the operation later prompted an investigation by the International Crimes Tribunal into possible crimes against humanity.

item.title: 3 arrested over attempted rape on moving bus in Ashulia
item.description:
Police have arrested three people, including a bus driver and his assistant, over the attempted rape of a woman aboard a moving bus in Ashulia, Dhaka.
The arrestees are bus helper Md Musfequr Rahman Joni, 20, driver Md Imran, 35, and Imran's acquaintance, Md Suman Pramanik, 30.
According to Ashulia police, the woman and her acquaintance, Md Rubel, 27, boarded a Savar Paribahan bus at Gabtoli in Dhaka around 1:30am on Sunday, intending to travel to Nabinagar in Savar.
As the bus neared Nabinagar, after other passengers had disembarked, driver Imran allegedly handed over the steering wheel to helper Joni. Police said Imran then assaulted Rubel, threatened to kill him, and forced him off the bus. Imran also got off shortly afterwards, leaving the woman, Joni and Suman on board.
Police alleged that Joni, with Suman's assistance, then attempted to rape the woman inside the moving bus. The victim screamed for help.
After getting off the bus, Rubel called the national emergency service 999 and informed police.
Acting on the information, Ashulia police intercepted the bus at Rarapara bus stand by blocking its path with another vehicle. The woman was rescued, while Joni and Suman were arrested at the scene.
The victim later filed a case under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act.
Police subsequently arrested driver Imran during a raid in the Baraipara area of Ashulia around 3:30pm on Sunday.
Ashulia Police Station Officer-in-Charge Mohammad Tariqul Islam said police responded immediately after receiving the 999 call, rescued the victim and arrested the suspects.
He said all three accused have been arrested in connection with the case.

item.title: Security guards vanish after Mirpur gold theft
item.description:
Around 259 bhori of gold jewellery was stolen from two jewellery shops at Shah Ali Shopping Complex in Mirpur, Dhaka, in the early hours of Sunday.
Police suspect the theft was carried out with the involvement of five market security guards, who have been missing since the incident.
According to Darus Salam police, the theft took place sometime between Saturday night and early Sunday.
The stolen jewellery belonged to Al Razzak Jewellers, owned by Jasim Uddin, and A Hossain Jewellers, owned by Abul Hossain, both located on the second floor of the shopping complex.
Darus Salam Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Dulal Hossain said preliminary findings suggest that around 200 bhori of gold ornaments were stolen from Al Razzak Jewellers and about 59 bhori from A Hossain Jewellers.
Describing it as a "well-planned theft," the OC said initial investigations indicate that the market's security guards were involved, along with three or four accomplices.
He said the guards had joined the market only a few days earlier with the intention of carrying out the theft.
Police also found that the national identity cards submitted by the guards during recruitment were fake, while their mobile phones have since been switched off.
The OC said police had obtained photographs of the suspects and were trying to identify them further by reviewing CCTV footage from the market.
According to investigators, security arrangements included both the market's own guards and a security guard assigned by the jewellery shops.
Police said the shop security guard was apparently rendered unconscious after being given sweets laced with a sedative.
CCTV footage also showed the market security guards allegedly taking part in the theft.
A case has been filed with Darus Salam Police Station. No arrests had been made as of 1am on Sunday.

item.title: Probe launched into 'poisoning' of water supply at Jungle Salimpur police outpost
item.description:
Police have launched an investigation after the water supply at the Alinagar Police Outpost in Chittagong's Jungle Salimpur was suspected to have been contaminated with poison or another toxic chemical substance.
The incident came to light on Sunday after three police personnel fell ill apparently after drinking water from the outpost.
Chittagong Superintendent of Police (SP) Md Masud Alam said personnel on duty noticed unusual foam and a strong stench in the water being used at the joint forces camp. Similar signs were later found in the camp's water tank, while an empty container believed to have contained a poisonous substance was recovered from the area.
"We cannot confirm yet whether it was poison, pesticide or any other chemical substance. The matter will be clear after receiving the laboratory report," he said.
Mohammad Mohinul Islam, Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Sitakunda Police Station, said three camp members noticed white foam while pouring water into a glass but did not initially consider it suspicious and drank the water. They later detected a strong chemical smell and soon fell ill.
The OC said the camp receives its drinking water through a pipeline connected to a nearby house.
Investigators suspect someone may have tampered with the supply line and mixed a chemical substance into the water.
Following the incident, water samples were collected and sent for laboratory testing, while the entire water tank was emptied and cleaned, he said, adding that the condition of the three affected police personnel is now stable and they are out of danger.
"The matter is under investigation," the OC said.
A temporary joint forces camp comprising personnel from the police, Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) has been established in the Salimpur jungle of Sitakunda, an area long regarded as a hideout for criminal and militant groups, to strengthen law and order.
On March 9, law enforcement agencies took control of the Salimpur jungle during a joint operation involving around 3,200 members of the Bangladesh Army, RAB, police and BGB.
Previous operations had failed to secure the area, with police and government officials coming under attack during earlier attempts.
On May 25, unidentified attackers targeted the joint forces camp under construction in the Alinagar area of Salimpur jungle, damaging it with an explosive device.
Later, a case was filed with Sitakunda Police Station over the incident, naming 242 people and accusing another 150 to 200 unidentified individuals.
However, the prime accused, Yasin, the alleged leader of the Yasin group, remains at large.

'Red Ivory' mango draws interest in Chapainawabganj
item.description:
In Bangladesh’s famed mango-producing district of Chapainawabganj, a striking crimson fruit is turning heads and drawing curious visitors, offering a glimpse of how exotic varieties could diversify the country's mango industry.
Rows of "Red Ivory" mangoes now hang in clusters from trees in a two-bigha orchard at Basantapur village in Shibganj upazila, where farmer Kabir Ali has successfully cultivated the foreign variety, attracting growers, students and fruit enthusiasts from across the district.
Known primarily as a vegetable farmer, Kabir's journey into cultivating the exotic mango began during a visit to Gaibandha, where he first encountered the Red Ivory variety. Impressed by its vibrant red colour, large size and commercial potential, he decided to bring the variety to his hometown.
Two years ago, he collected 340 saplings and established the orchard beside his home at a cost of around Tk150,000.
The trees produced fruit for the first time last year, yielding about five mounds of mangoes, which he sold at Tk5,500 per mound.
This season, however, nearly every tree has borne fruit.
Large crimson mangoes now cover the orchard, and the fruits are expected to reach the market within the next few weeks.
"Last year the harvest was small, but I received a good price. This year the trees are heavily laden with fruit. If the market price remains favourable, I hope to recover my investment and earn a profit," Kabir told UNB.
The unusual appearance of the mangoes has transformed Kabir's orchard into an attraction, with visitors arriving daily to see the rare variety firsthand.
Sanaullah, a local college student, said he had previously seen Red Ivory mangoes only on YouTube.
"Now I can see and even taste them in my own area. It's a wonderful experience. The mango looks beautiful and tastes excellent as well," he said.
Ataur Rahman, a mango grower from Laughatta area of Shibganj, said he visited the orchard after hearing about the foreign variety.
"The fruits are surprisingly large. Each mango appears to weigh between 800 grams and over one kilogram. The market value also seems promising. Seeing the orchard has inspired me to cultivate this variety next year," he said.
Another visitor, Robiul Islam from Chapainawabganj town, said he had also seen videos of the variety online but wanted to experience it in person.
"I am truly impressed after seeing the orchard with my own eyes," he said.
Habibur Rahman, who has been caring for the orchard since its establishment, said consumer response to the fruit was encouraging from the very beginning.
"When we harvested the first batch last year and took it to Kansat market, the mangoes sold out within a very short time," he said.
"We received a good price, and there was strong demand. This year almost every tree has produced fruit. We are hopeful of another successful season."
He added that people visit the orchard almost every day to learn more about the variety.
Deputy Director of the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE) in Chapainawabganj, Md Atikul Islam, said the district is home to more than 300 mango varieties, with growers increasingly showing interest in introducing foreign cultivars.
"The DAE is providing technical support and guidance to farmers who want to cultivate new varieties," he said.
According to the official, Red Ivory is a late-season variety, allowing growers to market the fruit after the peak mango season when supplies are lower and prices are generally higher.
He expressed optimism that Kabir Ali would benefit financially from this year's harvest
The success of Red Ivory cultivation is being seen as more than an individual achievement.
Local farmers and agricultural officials believe the variety could open new opportunities for Bangladesh's mango sector by extending the marketing season and introducing a premium fruit with strong consumer appeal.
If proper orchard management and marketing systems can be ensured, they say, the vivid red mango could emerge as a profitable addition to the country's expanding fruit industry while encouraging more growers to experiment with high-value exotic varieties.

item.title: Dhaka air quality remains moderate Monday morning
item.description:
Dhaka's air quality remained moderate on Monday morning, with an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 79.
The capital ranked 18th among the world's most polluted cities at 8:10 am, according to the AQI scale, while its air quality was classified as "moderate."
Pakistan’s Lahore, Uganda's Kampala and Indonesia’s Jakarta occupied the first three spots on the list with AQI scores of 195, 179 and 177, respectively.
An AQI between 50 and 100 is considered "moderate" with an acceptable air quality while AQI between 101 and 150 is considered ‘unhealthy for sensitive groups’, while a score between 151 and 200 is classified as ‘unhealthy’. AQI readings between 201 and 300 are termed ‘very unhealthy’, and anything above 301 is considered ‘hazardous’, posing serious health risks.
The AQI is a daily indicator of air quality, showing how clean or polluted the air is and the possible health effects people may experience.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide, carbon monoxide, sulphur dioxide and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with severe air pollution. Air quality usually worsens during winter and improves in the monsoon season.
According to the World Health Organization, air pollution causes around seven million deaths globally each year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic respiratory diseases, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: Health minister visits Tala Health Complex, promises upgrade to 100-bed hospital
item.description:
Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Hossain made a surprise visit to Tala Upazila Health Complex in Satkhira on Sunday, inspecting hospital facilities and pledging to upgrade the facility to a 100-bed hospital.
Arriving at around 10:30 am, the minister began his inspection in the hospital kitchen, where he sampled food prepared for patients to assess its quality. He later toured the male and female wards, medicine store, operating theatre (OT), administrative offices, washrooms, and staff attendance registers.
During the visit, he met patients to hear their views on medical treatment, medicine availability, and the overall quality of healthcare services. He also inspected the hospital premises and discussed service challenges and future development plans with local residents and officials.
The minister instructed hospital authorities to improve healthcare services and ordered action against those responsible for the theft of air-conditioning units from the hospital. He also directed officials to expedite ongoing renovation work, including improvements to washroom facilities and called for administrative action against a medical officer who has reportedly remained absent from duty for an extended period.
Speaking to reporters after the visit, Hossain said the government is continuing to recruit doctors through a special Bangladesh Civil Service (BCS) process to address staffing shortages. He added that the recruitment process for 100,000 healthcare workers has also begun.
The minister announced that work to upgrade Tala Upazila Health Complex to a 100-bed facility will begin soon, with soil testing expected in the coming weeks.
He said the project includes constructing a modern seven-to- eight-storey building equipped with separate paralysis rehabilitation centers for men and women, a physiotherapy center, a breastfeeding corner, and a trauma center to strengthen healthcare services for the region.

item.title: Jamuna erosion keeps Tangail regional road cut off for 6th day
item.description:
Traffic on the Tangail–Bhuapur–Tarakandi regional road remained suspended for the sixth consecutive day yesterday as repair work on a section washed away by erosion from the Jamuna River continued, causing widespread disruption and raising fears of further collapse.
The erosion began suddenly last Sunday at Sakharia village in Gopalpur upazila, where strong currents from the Jamuna River swept away an initial 25-metre stretch of the road. The damaged section has since widened to about 80 metres.
The road closure has halted the movement of passenger buses, freight vehicles and ambulances, forcing commuters and transport operators to use longer alternative routes. The detours have increased travel time, transportation costs and hardship for residents.
People living near the affected area have begun moving household belongings and livestock to safer locations amid concerns that further erosion could breach the remaining road and allow river water to inundate nearby settlements.
Officials from the Bangladesh Water Development Board (BWDB) are carrying out emergency protection work by dumping geo bags and tube bags along the eroding riverbank in an effort to stabilise the area.
Locals said they remain anxious despite the ongoing work, warning that failure to contain the erosion quickly could lead to extensive damage to homes, agricultural land and critical infrastructure.
"We are living in constant fear," said local resident Nazrul Islam. "If the road collapses completely, vast areas of Gopalpur, Bhuapur and the greater Mymensingh region could be affected."
Another resident, Md Hayrat, said villagers have been unable to sleep peacefully due to fears that the erosion could destroy their homes and farmland.
A resident named Anowara said her family had already moved their cattle to safer ground and feared they would have nowhere to go if the road gave way completely.
BWDB Executive Engineer Main Uddin attributed the erosion to heavy rainfall, strong upstream flows and changes in the Jamuna's channel caused by the formation of sandbars, which redirected the river's current towards the road.
"The affected section remains vulnerable. Geo bag dumping operations are continuing and will remain in place until the situation is brought under control," he said.
Local lawmaker Abdus Salam Pintu said emergency erosion-control measures were launched immediately after the collapse and that the government, BWDB and local residents were working together to prevent further damage.
The state minister for fisheries and livestock said more than 25,000 geo bags, along with large pipe bags, had already been deployed to reinforce the riverbank. He added that the government was also pursuing plans for a permanent embankment and hoped the emergency repair work would be completed soon.

item.title: Dev projects in Dumuria face uncertainty amid funding crisis
item.description:
Development projects worth around Tk1.70 crore in Dumuria Upazila of Khulna are facing uncertainty as the upazila administration’s development fund has almost run out of money.
The fund crisis has put several projects, including rural road construction, tube wells, religious institutions, educational facilities and other public infrastructure works, at risk of cancellation.
According to the upazila administration records, the development fund had a balance of Tk7.15 crore on 30 July 2025, while the revenue fund stood at Tk35 lakh .
However, at a meeting held on 21 May this year, officials said the balance in the development fund had dropped to only Tk3,729, while the revenue fund had increased to Tk3.30 core.
The figures show that nearly Tk7.15 crore was spent from the development fund within ten months, raising questions among local stakeholders over the utilisation of the money.
Meanwhile, the Upazila Engineering Department’s development projects worth Tk1.70 crore for the 2025–26 fiscal year are now at risk of being stalled due to the shortage of funds.
Contractors have already stopped 54 projects under seven packages, involving around Tk 80 lakh, after failing to receive work orders despite winning tenders through a lottery process held on 21 May.
Some contractors said they had completed assigned works and submitted bills, but later found that there was no money available in the development fund for payment.
The affected projects include road development, tube wells, mosques, temples, madrasas, educational institutions and paving works. Projects worth another Tk90 lakh are still at the tender invitation stage.
Sheikh Shahinur Rahman, president of the Dumuria Upazila Contractor Welfare Association, said contractors had suffered financial losses after spending money to participate in the tender process.
“More than 100 contractors submitted bids for projects under the Upazila Engineering Department. Each contractor spent around Tk7,500 on the tender process. Many won projects through the lottery, but work orders have not been issued,” he said.
He added that a meeting between contractors and the Upazila Executive Officer was held, but no solution had been found.
Dumuria Upazila Engineer Muhammad Darul Huda said the tender process was completed following government regulations, including newspaper advertisements and a lottery system.
“Work orders cannot be issued because there is no money available in the upazila development fund,” he said.
Upazila Executive Officer Sabita Sarkar said issuing work orders without sufficient funds would create further complications.
“If contractors are given work orders, they will complete the projects and submit bills. But there is no money in the fund to pay them,” she said.
Md Kamrul Islam Sardar, executive engineer of the Local Government Engineering Department (LGED), Khulna, said several projects under the 2025–26 fiscal year had been affected due to the fund shortage.
“If work orders are issued without available funds, contractors will complete the work and later face difficulties getting their payments,” he said.
The shortage of funds has raised concerns that important development activities in Dumuria may remain stalled unless additional financial support is arranged.

item.title: Govt primary school enrolment falls in Rajshahi
item.description:
Enrolment in government primary schools across Rajshahi division has declined over the past 12 years despite population growth, while private kindergartens and madrasas have continued to attract more students, according to official data.
Figures from the Divisional Deputy Director's Office of Primary Education show that student enrolment in government primary schools dropped from 1,320,975 in 2014 to 1,183,992 in 2026, a decline of 136,983. During the same period, the population of Rajshahi division increased by around 2.5 million.
In contrast, enrolment in private primary schools, including kindergartens, rose from 436,966 to 504,030 students. Officials also said admissions to Alia and Qawmi madrasas have increased steadily, although consolidated enrolment data were unavailable.
Educationists say the shift reflects growing concerns among parents about the quality of education in government schools, as well as stronger confidence in private institutions.
Head teachers across the division said the rapid expansion of kindergartens and madrasas has contributed significantly to declining enrolment in government schools.
Afroza Khatun, head teacher of Kantanagar Government Primary School in Bagmara upazila, said the school's enrolment had fallen from around 100 students to about 60 after two kindergartens opened nearby.
At Atkoshi Government Primary School in Rajshahi city, enrolment has dropped from more than 550 students five years ago to around 350, according to head teacher Nilufa Akhtar Khanam.
"There are at least 10 kindergarten schools and several madrasas within one kilometre of our school. Many students have transferred there," she said.
Teachers from more than two dozen government primary schools interviewed by this correspondent reported similar trends, with many citing increased admissions to nearby kindergartens and madrasas.
Nikhil Ranjan Pramanik, a teacher at Kachua-2 Government Primary School in Tanore upazila, said 17 students recently left his school to enrol in a nearby madrasa.
"We are trying to improve the quality of education, but admissions continue to decline every year," he said.
Parents said they preferred kindergartens because of regular assessments, closer teacher supervision, better communication with families and greater emphasis on English-language education.
"Government schools are free, but we are not satisfied with the quality of education," said Mustafizur Rahman, a parent in Rajshahi city. "Kindergarten teachers closely monitor children and regularly update parents on their progress."
Another guardian, Saju, whose son attends Shaheen School in Rajshahi, said he chose a private school because he believed it offered better-quality education and stronger English instruction.
Domestic worker Asma Begum said she enrolled her daughter in a kindergarten despite financial hardship because she wanted her to receive a better education.
Professor Dr Akhter Banu, director of the Institute of Education and Research at Rajshahi University, said parents ultimately choose schools they trust.
"Even many government primary school teachers prefer to enrol their own children in private schools instead of the schools where they teach. That reflects declining confidence in the public education system," she said.
She said weak supervision, limited teacher motivation and a lack of accountability have undermined public trust, while private schools maintain closer communication with parents.
"Unless supervision, accountability and teacher motivation improve, parents will continue to shift their children to other institutions," she added.
Nur Akhtar Jannatul Ferdous, assistant director at the Rajshahi Divisional Deputy Director's Office of Primary Education, said more research was needed to determine the reasons behind the decline in enrolment.
"It is not possible to identify a single reason at this stage. A detailed study is needed to understand the factors involved," she said.

item.title: Tangail bridge approach damaged by heavy rainfall
item.description:
Heavy rainfall has damaged a section of the approach to a bridge by the Local Government Engineering Department (LGED) at Shyamar Ghat on the Tangail–Hugra road in Tangail Sadar upazila, making vehicular movement risky.
On Sunday afternoon, LGED Executive Engineer Jahanara Parvin, who recently joined the district, inspected the damaged bridge approach and said repairs would be carried out soon.
According to residents, a section of the bridge approach collapsed during the current monsoon season due to heavy rainfall, creating risks for vehicles crossing the bridge.
The bridge is used daily by thousands of people from Hugra, Dyenna, Katuli and Kakua in the char areas of Tangail Sadar upazila, as well as Chauhali in Sirajganj district. Residents said the same section of the approach had collapsed several times in the past and called for a permanent solution.
After being informed about the damage, Jahanara Parvin visited the site and inspected the affected area.
She said: “The bridge approach was damaged due to heavy rainfall. After the inspection, the matter has been reported to the higher authorities. We hope the repairs will be completed quickly so that the bridge becomes suitable for vehicular movement.”
LGED Sub-Assistant Engineer Mostafizur Rahman and other department officials were present during the inspection.
The bridge was constructed around 15 years ago to improve transportation for residents of the surrounding char areas.

item.title: HC sets Aug 2 for verdict on Chinmoy’s bail in 2 cases

item.title: SDF seeks ICT probe into Shahabuddin's alleged role in July killings
item.description:
The State Dialogue Forum (SDF) has submitted a petition to the International Crimes Tribunal, seeking an investigation into the alleged role of former president Mohammed Shahabuddin in the killings during the July 2024 mass uprising, as well as enforced disappearances and torture during the Awami League's rule.
The petition was submitted to the Chief Prosecutor on Sunday by the forum's central member secretary, Al Noor Mohammad Ayas.
In the petition, Ayas alleged that he was abducted by masked men from the Mohakhali bus terminal on the night of January 18, 2025, after leading protests at Shahbagh demanding Shahabuddin's resignation. He claimed he was subjected to physical and psychological torture and was forced to record a video message calling for the suspension of the movement.
According to the petition, he was abandoned near the Kawran Bazar-Banglamotor area the following day and was later rescued and admitted to Dhaka Medical College Hospital.
Ayas also urged the tribunal to investigate Shahabuddin's alleged role as an instigator of the shootings, killings, enforced disappearances and other alleged human rights abuses against students and civilians during the July 2024 mass uprising.
He further called for an impartial and independent investigation into Shahabuddin's constitutional role and responsibilities as the then president, as well as whether he bore any legal liability or involvement in the 2024 election, alleged human rights violations, and events related to the mass uprising.

item.title: Gas crisis deepens as LNG terminal outage disrupts supply, cripples household cooking
item.description:
The ongoing gas crisis, triggered by a fire at a floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU) in Cox’s Bazar, is unlikely to ease anytime soon, leaving millions of households in Dhaka and surrounding areas struggling to cook.
The accident has reduced the country's total gas supply to below 2,150 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd), down from an average of around 2,700 mmcfd that had been maintained over the past year, despite the national daily demand standing at nearly 3,800 mmcfd.
The fire at the FSRU operated by Excelerate Energy at Moheshkhali on Tuesday damaged one of its two boilers, forcing it to suspend operations, further plummeting the gas supply.
International expert teams from the UK and the United Arab Emirates have been working at the terminal since Thursday to repair the technical damage.
Tariqul Islam Khan, public relations officer of Bangladesh Oil, Gas and Mineral Corporation (Petrobangla), indicated that while efforts are underway, it will take more time before the facility can resume operation.
The severe supply shortfall has hit domestic kitchens the hardest, with gas pressure dropping to near zero or flickering feebly in many parts of the capital.
Residents in areas such as Mohammadpur, Kalabagan, Kafrul, Kazipara, West Tejturi Bazar, Mirpur, Rampura and Badda reported that stoves have remained unlit or unusable for days.
Stripped of regular gas supply, many low-income families have been forced to build temporary clay stoves and cook with firewood. Others who can afford it are turning to costly electric cookers or LPG cylinders, significantly increasing their daily household expenses.
Frustrated residents in several neighbourhoods, including Mohammadpur, have staged demonstrations and vented their anger on social media platforms over the persistent cooking crisis.
Beyond domestic kitchens, the shortage has severely impacted other sectors.
According to Petrobangla, gas-fired electricity generation has fallen by approximately 1,500 megawatts, raising concerns over widespread power cuts.
Long queues of vehicles have formed at CNG filling stations across the city, while industrial production has slowed down due to low gas pressure.
Petrobangla issued a statement apologising to consumers for the unexpected disruption and assured that technical teams are working continuously to restore the terminal.
Meanwhile, Titas Gas Transmission and Distribution PLC warned that low gas pressure will persist across Dhaka and adjacent districts until the situation improves.

item.title: Bangladeshi artist wins gold prize at World Beauty Art & Design International Contest
item.description:
Bangladeshi artist Sayma Sadia won the gold prize in the Makeup – General Category at the 25th World Beauty Art & Design International Contest, held in Seoul, South Korea.
Organized by the World Beauty Art Association, the annual competition brings together beauty artists, educators, and professionals from around the world to showcase their work in makeup, beauty, and artistic design.
According to officials at the award ceremony, Sayma received the gold prize in recognition of her artistic skill, creativity, and technical expertise in the Makeup – General Category.
Sayma is currently pursuing a bachelor's degree in Beauty Design at Woosong University in South Korea. She said the award marked a significant milestone in her career and encouraged her to pursue higher goals in the global beauty industry.
She hopes to work with internationally recognized beauty and cosmetics brands while specializing in Special Effects (SFX) Makeup, a field widely used in film, television, fashion, and theater.
Speaking about the achievement, Sayma said: “I feel deeply honored and grateful to receive this recognition. Winning the gold prize is not just my achievement, it belongs to everyone who has supported me throughout my journey. At this moment, I especially remember my parents and my sister, whose love, encouragement, and sacrifices have helped me reach this stage. Their belief in me has always been my greatest strength.”
Her achievement reflects the growing presence of Bangladeshi talent in international beauty and design competitions and highlights the country's expanding participation in the global creative industry.

Faridpur farmers expect bumper jute harvest, seek fair prices
item.description:
Farmers in Faridpur are busy harvesting and retting jute cultivated on 87,000 hectares this season, with favourable weather boosting hopes of bumper yield. However, growers remain concerned over rising production costs and uncertainty surrounding market prices.
According to the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE), nearly 90% of farmers in the district cultivated jute this season. The production target has been set at 195,000 metric tonnes, with an expected average yield of 2.24 metric tonnes per hectare.
DAE Deputy Director Shahaduzzaman said favourable weather conditions throughout the growing season have increased the likelihood of achieving the production target.
"We are optimistic about meeting this season's target as weather conditions have remained favourable for jute cultivation," he said.
He added that Faridpur contributes around 30% of the country's total jute production, with the district's fibre widely recognised for its quality.
Despite the positive production outlook, farmers say higher input costs have squeezed their profit margins. Limited rainfall at the beginning of the season forced many to irrigate their fields, while rising prices of fertilisers, fuel and other agricultural inputs increased cultivation expenses. Labour costs have also continued to climb.
Farmers in Saltha, including Hasem Matubbar, Harun Molla and Saiful Islam, said they are currently harvesting and retting their crop but fear incurring losses if they do not receive fair prices at the end of the season.
They urged the government to procure jute at the announced price on time and improve market management to ensure fair returns, saying such measures would encourage farmers to expand jute cultivation.
Faridpur Farmers' Association President Manik Majumdar said strong production alone would not guarantee farmers' livelihoods.
"Ensuring fair prices, improving market access and reducing production costs are essential to making jute cultivation profitable," he said. "That will help preserve Faridpur's position as one of Bangladesh's leading jute-producing districts."

item.title: Heavy rains push up vegetable, fish prices in Gopalganj
item.description:
Prices of vegetables in Gopalganj have doubled or even tripled over the past 10 days following heavy rainfall that damaged crops and disrupted supplies, leaving low and middle-income families struggling to cope with soaring food costs.
A visit to Boro Bazar in the town showed that no vegetable was selling for less than Tk 60 per kilogram. Okra, previously priced at Tk 20-25 per kg, is now selling for Tk 60. Sweet pumpkin price has increased from Tk 25-30 to Tk 60, while pointed gourd, ridge gourd and teasel gourd are selling at Tk 80 per kg after rising sharply from Tk 30-35. Sponge gourd now costs Tk 60, and both bitter gourd and taro corms have reached Tk 80 per kg.
A medium-sized bottle gourd that recently sold for Tk 30-40 now costs Tk 80-100. Papaya remains the cheapest vegetable at Tk 40 per kg, while green chilies have jumped to Tk 200 per kg from Tk 80 just 10 days ago.
Fish prices have also climbed significantly. Hilsa weighing one kilogram is selling for nearly Tk 3,000, while smaller hilsa weighing 350-400 grams costs around Tk 1,500. Farmed varieties, including pangas, rohit, catla and silver carp, have become Tk 25-50 more expensive per kilogram. Rohit now sells for Tk 500-600 per kg, up from Tk 450-480 only a few days ago.
Fish trader Johor blamed the increase on heavy rains in fish-producing areas, saying floodwaters caused farmed fish to escape from ponds, reducing market supply. Although hilsa prices briefly declined last week due to increased seasonal catches, they have since risen again, pushing overall fish prices higher.
Consumers say the rising costs are placing severe pressure on household budgets. Shopper Saidul Islam Shovon said many families can no longer afford to buy all the essentials. Another customer, Md. Ehsanul Alam, said his family has reduced fish consumption because prices continue to rise while incomes remain unchanged.
Vegetable traders said continuous rainfall has damaged crops and sharply reduced supplies reaching wholesale markets. They noted that vegetable prices usually increase during the monsoon season, but this year's prolonged rainfall has made the situation far worse.
Dr. Md. Mamunur Rahman, Deputy Director of the Department of Agricultural Extension in Gopalganj, said above-normal rainfall in July inundated 85 hectares of vegetable fields, damaging crops including bitter gourd, bottle gourd, pumpkin, papaya, pointed gourd, okra, chili and yardlong beans. The losses have affected 1,360 vegetable farmers and significantly reduced local market supplies.
District Agricultural Marketing Officer Arif Hossain said authorities are continuing regular market monitoring and have advised traders to avoid excessive profit-taking while maintaining reasonable margins between wholesale and retail prices.
He added that with local production declining, most vegetables are now being brought into Gopalganj from other districts, contributing to higher prices.

item.title: Youth found dead at Hasina’s residence Sudha Sadan in Dhanmondi
item.description:
Police recovered the hanging body of a 20-year-old man from Sudha Sadan, the former residence of ex-prime minister Sheikh Hasina in the Dhanmondi area of the capital on Saturday.
The deceased was identified as Shakil, son of Sekandar Ali Matubbar and Asma Begum. He lived in the Shibpur Tile Office area of Jigatola under Mohammadpur.
Police said the body was recovered at around 11am after locals informed them. It was later sent to the Dhaka Medical College Hospital morgue for an autopsy following due procedures.
Md Waduzzaman, sub-inspector (SI) of Dhanmondi Police Station, said the body was found hanging with a noose around the neck.
He said the Crime Scene Unit of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) identified the deceased through fingerprint analysis.
The exact cause of death has not yet been determined, and an investigation is underway, the police officer added.

item.title: Pipe bomb planted to target Rath Yatra
item.description:
The Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit said the pipe bomb had been planted to target the Ulto Rath Yatra procession after police recovered the powerful improvised explosive device (IED) beneath Motijheel Metro Rail Station in Dhaka on Friday.
Sub-Inspector (SI) Mirza Mohammad Mukta of Motijheel Police Station subsequently filed a case under the Explosives Act against unidentified individuals
According to the case, police received information about a suspicious bomb-like object along the procession route and recovered an umbrella containing a powerful pipe bomb before the religious procession reached the area. Authorities said the device was detected in time, preventing a potentially serious incident.
A passerby was injured during the controlled disposal of the bomb on Friday night. The injured, 66-year-old Miraj Ahmed, an employee of the Ministry of Education, sustained splinter injuries to his left eye. After receiving primary treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital, he was referred to the National Institute of Ophthalmology in Agargaon for further treatment.
According to the case documents, SI Mirza Mohammad Mukta was on duty with the "Honda Mobile" patrol unit to provide security for the Ulto Rath Yatra procession.
The procession began at Dhakeshwari National Temple, passed through Shapla Chattar in Motijheel and was scheduled to conclude at Swamibagh Ashram.
During the evening, the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Control Room received information from the Traffic Division about a suspicious bomb-like object near the procession route. The device had been concealed inside an umbrella, and witnesses reported seeing a blinking light on it.
Following instructions from senior officials, SI Mukta and other officers reached the area beside the generator room of Motijheel Metro Rail Station at around 6:20pm and secured the location where the device had been found.
Police then requested participants in the procession to avoid the area, telling them there had been an electrical short circuit, allowing the procession to continue safely toward Swamibagh Ashram.
After the procession had passed through the area, members of the DMP Bomb Disposal Unit carried out a controlled explosion and safely neutralized the device, according to the case.
Speaking to Dhaka Tribune on Saturday evening, Additional Commissioner of Dhaka Metropolitan Police and chief of the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit Mohammad Shamsul Haque said: "The powerful pipe bomb had been planted to target the Rath Yatra procession."
He said the explosive had been attached to an umbrella in a way that opening it would have triggered the blast, potentially causing multiple casualties.
Describing the device, he said: "It was an improvised explosive device (IED) in the form of a pipe bomb. It contained sulfur, a large quantity of sharp metal fragments and barbed wire. The device was connected to a battery and an electrical circuit and was designed so that pressing the release button to open the umbrella would detonate the bomb."
Shamsul Haque confirmed that one passerby was injured during the bomb disposal operation and said the casualties could have been much higher had the area been crowded.
He added that investigators have yet to identify those responsible or determine their motive. He urged the public not to panic, saying law enforcement agencies and other relevant authorities are investigating the incident to identify and apprehend those involved.

item.title: 439 fresh cases of dengue infection reported, 1 death overnight

According to Article 54 of the Constitution, Speaker of the National Parliament Hafiz Uddin Ahmad Bir Bikram will discharge the duties of the president of the People's Republic of Bangladesh until a new president is elected.
The provision came into effect following the resignation of President Mohammed Sahabuddin from office on Friday.
